level_problem: Past perfect for an unfulfilled plan is a C1 point, but 'was/have' are weak distractors; only 'had planned' is even grammatical, so a B1 learner gets it by elimination.

answer: we were hoping you might help us with the move
other_correct: were we hoping you might help us with the move (question; grammatical but pragmatically odd)
level_problem: Tentative past continuous 'we were hoping' is B1/B2; easy for C1.
Annoying past habit with 'always' + past continuous is B2; 'has/is' are rejected instantly by 'When we were teenagers'. Easy for C1.

answer: we were walking to work every day during the strike
other_correct: during the strike we were walking to work every day
every day during the strike we were walking to work
during the strike, every day we were walking to work (less natural)
we were walking to work during the strike every day (less natural)
were we walking to work every day during the strike (question)
level_problem: Past continuous for a temporary repeated situation is fine for C1 but the ordering itself is easy.
sense_problem: Many correct orders because of the two movable adverbials; the key must accept them. 'We walked to work' would be the more natural choice; past continuous is fine only as a temporary-situation reading.

level_problem: Past perfect continuous for visible evidence is B2; the cards leave only one grammatical string. A B1/B2 learner solves it at once.
Interrupted past continuous is A2/B1; far too easy for C1 ('had' gives only *had wrote/*had writing).
sense_problem: Distractor 'had' produces no real form ('had wrote', 'had writing'), so it is not a believable C1 mistake; 'had written' would be the real competitor.

answer: i was going to call you but i fell asleep
other_correct: i fell asleep but i was going to call you (grammatical, less logical order)
level_problem: 'was going to' for an unrealised intention is B1; too easy for C1.
Personal passive with perfect infinitive is B2/C1, acceptable.

answer: this is the third time the lift has broken down this month
other_correct: this is the third time this month the lift has broken down

level_problem: Four gaps leave only one grammatical string; fine for B2/C1 but mechanical.
Present perfect after 'once' for future completion is B1/B2; easy.
sense_problem: 'will submitted' is not a real form, so 'will' is a weak distractor; the believable mistake would be 'will submit' or 'will have submitted'.

answer: i've been trying to reach you all afternoon
other_correct: all afternoon i've been trying to reach you (fronted, less natural)
level_problem: Present perfect continuous with 'all afternoon' is B1; too easy for C1.
Present perfect with 'this week' is A2/B1; far too easy for C1.
sense_problem: 'was received' is passive and nonsensical here; weak distractor.

answer: the house is thought to have been built in the 1890s
other_correct: is the house thought to have been built in the 1890s (question)

level_problem: Fine for C1 ('should' in a conditional), though 'will/would/had' are rejected quickly.

answer: when she was a child she would spend hours in the garden
other_correct: she would spend hours in the garden when she was a child
sense_problem: Two equally correct clause orders; key must accept both.
Good C1 item (insistent 'will' in if-clause). Note some learners may find 'If you will go' unfamiliar; that is the point. No other combination works.

answer: the car wouldn't start this morning so i took the bus
other_correct: this morning the car wouldn't start so i took the bus
the car wouldn't start so i took the bus this morning
this morning the car wouldn't start, so i took the bus
the car wouldn't start so this morning i took the bus (less natural)
level_problem: 'wouldn't' for refusal of a machine is B1/B2; easy.
sense_problem: 'this morning' can go in at least three places; key must accept them.
Good. 'will be' after 'in case' is a real learner error (non-standard), so a good distractor; strict BrE rejects it.

answer: you should have told me you were going to be late

level_problem: Fixed phrase; fine for C1, though only 'might as' is possible with the cards.

answer: he can't have been at home last night
other_correct: last night he can't have been at home (fronted, less natural)
can't he have been at home last night (negative question, marginal)

level_problem: 'can' for typical behaviour is B1/B2; easy for C1.
Too easy: the could/were allowed contrast is not tested because 'could' cannot fill two gaps (*could allowed). Only a B1 passive is needed.
sense_problem: Distractor 'could' gives no real form here, so it is not a believable mistake; the item looks as if it wants the 'could vs was able/allowed' point but does not test it.

answer: she may be clever but she has no common sense
other_correct: she has no common sense but she may be clever (grammatical, weaker concessive meaning)

level_problem: 'could see' with a sense verb is A2/B1; far too easy.
sense_problem: 'managed' cannot combine with any card into a real form (*managed see/saw), so it is not a believable distractor; 'managed to see' would need 'to'.

answer: they might have been delayed by the snow
other_correct: might they have been delayed by the snow (question)
drink
no
drinks
no
wrong_options_that_fit: 'drink no coffee' is a correct (less natural) mandative subjunctive; 'drinks no coffee' is acceptable British English after 'recommend that' (Hewings/Swan: BrE allows the ordinary present).
sense_problem: Seriously ambiguous: the cards 'no' and 'drinks' combine into two further correct answers. Remove 'no' or replace with a non-form.

answer: i'd rather you had asked me before taking my car
other_correct: before taking my car i'd rather you had asked me (fronted, awkward)

answer: the committee insisted that the decision be made public
other_correct: the public insisted that the committee decision be made (grammatical, sensible: 'committee decision' as noun compound)
the decision insisted that the committee be made public (grammatical but absurd)
sense_problem: Ambiguous: 'the public insisted that the committee decision be made' uses all cards and makes sense. Key must accept it or the cards must change.

answer: the landlord requested that all tenants should leave their keys at reception
other_correct: the landlord requested that tenants should leave all their keys at reception
all tenants requested that the landlord should leave their keys at reception (grammatical, plausible)
sense_problem: 'all' is movable ('all their keys') and subject/object roles can swap; at least two other correct sentences.

level_problem: 'news' + singular verb is B1; easy for C1.

answer: the majority of the residents are against the new car park
other_correct: the majority of the new residents are against the car park
sense_problem: 'new' can attach to 'residents'; second fully natural answer.

other_correct: still
makes
wrong_options_that_fit: 'makes' (singular after 'one of the ... who') is widespread and accepted in informal usage (Swan); strictly plural 'make' is correct.
sense_problem: Key should decide whether 'still makes' is tolerated; strict teachers reject it, many native speakers use it.

other_correct: has
been
wrong_options_that_fit: 'There has been three cars' is non-standard but very common in speech ('there's been'); strict answer rejects it.
level_problem: Fine for B2/C1.

answer: two thirds of the money has already been spent
other_correct: two thirds of the money has been spent already
already two thirds of the money has been spent
sense_problem: 'already' is movable; key must accept the alternatives.

answer: neither the teacher nor the students were happy with the results
other_correct: neither the students nor the teacher were happy with the results (common, but strict proximity rule wants 'was')
sense_problem: Swapping teacher/students gives a sentence that is widespread but prescriptively wrong; decide and document.

answer: this is the problem we need to deal with
other_correct: the problem we need to deal with is this
is this the problem we need to deal with (question)
level_problem: Stranded preposition in a contact clause is B1/B2; easy.
sense_problem: Reverse order 'the problem we need to deal with is this' is fully correct.

level_problem: Easy for C1; 'despite of' is a good real error though.

answer: the matter is being looked into by the police
other_correct: is the matter being looked into by the police (question)

level_problem: 'insist on -ing' is B1/B2; easy.

answer: she's not an easy person to work with

sense_problem: Fine; 'Reading' alone would also be possible English ('Reading the email, she deleted it') but cannot fill two gaps.

answer: not wanting to wake the children we spoke in whispers
other_correct: we spoke in whispers, not wanting to wake the children
wanting not to wake the children, we spoke in whispers (grammatical, less natural)
sense_problem: Participle clause can go before or after the main clause; key must accept both.
Absolute construction is correct but formal/literary for such an everyday sentence ('As the weather was bad' is what people say).

answer: the woman sitting next to me on the plane was a famous actress
other_correct: the woman sitting on the plane next to me was a famous actress
the woman on the plane sitting next to me was a famous actress (less natural)
the actress sitting next to me on the plane was a famous woman (grammatical, odd)
level_problem: Reduced relative clause is B2; 13 cards make it long but not hard.
sense_problem: Adverbial phrases are movable; several correct orders.

answer: generally speaking people here are very friendly
other_correct: speaking generally, people here are very friendly
people here are, generally speaking, very friendly
people here, generally speaking, are very friendly
people here are very friendly, generally speaking
level_problem: Easy for C1.
sense_problem: Very many correct orders; 'speaking generally' also exists. Hard to key.

answer: no sooner had the film started than the power went off
other_correct: the film had no sooner started than the power went off
sense_problem: Uninverted 'the film had no sooner started than...' uses all cards and is correct (Hewings lists it); key must accept it.

answer: at the top of the hill stands an old church
other_correct: an old church stands at the top of the hill
sense_problem: If the target is locative inversion, the uninverted order is equally correct and more neutral; the task cannot force inversion.

answer: all we need now is a bit of luck
other_correct: now all we need is a bit of luck
all we need is a bit of luck now
a bit of luck is all we need now
a bit of luck is all we now need (less natural)
sense_problem: 'now' is movable and the cleft can be reversed; many correct answers.

level_problem: 'be being + adjective' is B2; acceptable.

answer: we're hoping you can join us for dinner on saturday
other_correct: we're hoping you can join us on saturday for dinner
on saturday we're hoping you can join us for dinner (less natural)
level_problem: B1 level structure; easy for C1.
sense_problem: Adverbials movable.

level_problem: Present continuous for a developing situation is B1/B2.
Present 'tells/says' for passing on news is B2; easy.

answer: we're loving every minute of our holiday
level_problem: Stative 'love' in continuous is B2; the order is trivial, B1 solves at once.

answer: so i'm standing at the bus stop and this man comes up to me
other_correct: i'm standing at the bus stop and so this man comes up to me (grammatical, odd)
sense_problem: Fine anecdotal present; 14 cards is long.

level_problem: Present simple for commentary/demonstration is B1; the past-tense distractors are rejected by 'And now'. Too easy.
